title: Streaming chunked token double-counted during reconnects - urgent billing escalation
creator: Elena Martinez
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported unexpectedly high token usage on recent invoices. Root cause appears limited to streaming/multipart responses where intermittent client reconnects or chunk-resend behavior caused per-chunk accounting to be logged as independent token usage events. This impacts hosted, dedicated, and private deployments that use the streaming aggregation path. Immediate priority is to stop further overcounting, quantify affected invoices, and prepare reconciliations and refunds where applicable.
reproduction_steps: 1) Open a streaming text_generation call (stream=true) to a long-response model (~ > 2k tokens expected).
2) Simulate an intermittent network drop after receiving a few chunks and reconnect the client socket/resume streaming with a fresh session id, or resend prior chunk boundaries.
3) Observe server metrics: two distinct token-accounting events emitted for the same logical response (chunk A repeated with new session id), leading to duplicated token counts in the usage pipeline.
4) Confirm by inspecting raw broker logs and the token-accumulator stream that session_id or request_id normalization failed before dedup step.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 - Elena: Customer report received from Account team (acct-rapid) for 3 high-dollar invoices showing +15-40% above expected usage. Escalated to SRE and runtime teams.

2026-03-02 - Ravi: Reproduced locally using a custom client that tears down and reopens the streaming connection. Observed duplicate token-accounting messages emitted to the ingestion topic when session_id changed mid-response.

2026-03-03 - Grace Lin (SRE): Traced ingestion timeline: aggregator service was deduping on (request_id, model, timestamp-window) but streaming reconnects used a different request_id, bypassing dedupe. The KV-cache reuse path did not include a stable logical_request_id header.

2026-03-04 - Runtime: Identified three code paths that emit accounting events: (1) per-chunk post-processing, (2) finalize-on-close, (3) reconnect-resume handler. We are double-emitting when (1) and (3) both run without normalized request_id.
2026-03-05 - PM Paul Nguyen: Confirmed affected customers include two hosted SOC2 customers and one Dedicated customer in us-west with streaming-heavy integrations (web-sockets for chat UIs).
impact_summary: High-severity overbilling for customers using streaming APIs with reconnect/resume logic. Preliminary sample (3 customers) shows billing inflation between 12-38% for streaming-dominant workloads. This is a direct revenue-risk / customer satisfaction issue.
mitigation_steps_taken: 2026-03-05 - Hotfix: Disabled the streaming-reconnect aggregation fallback that emitted duplicate accounting events (temp toggle on aggregator via feature-flag). This stops new duplicate events but does not retroactively change already-ingested events.
2026-03-06 - Monitoring: Added alerts on per-customer streaming token delta > historical baseline + 10% and a dashboard to track duplicate-low-entropy request_id patterns.
2026-03-07 - Support: Notified affected account teams and started a watchlist for other customers with streaming-heavy patterns.
2026-03-08 - Rollout: Deployed a normalization patch to set a stable logical_request_id on streaming-resume in runtime (canary on dedicated cluster A).
root_cause_analysis: A combination of two issues: (1) streaming client reconnects used a new session/request identifier which prevented deduplication in the ingestion pipeline; (2) the runtime emitted per-chunk accounting events on both chunk-send and on-resume finalization, leading to counts being recorded twice when reconnects occurred. The dedupe window logic assumed idempotent request_ids and did not normalize across resume boundaries.
resolution_summary: Patched runtime to attach a stable logical_request_id to streaming sessions (preserves across reconnects per RFC-style resume token). Updated aggregator to dedupe on logical_request_id + chunk-offset. Hotfixed feature-flag removed. Full rollout targeted to all clusters by 2026-03-12. Backfill/reconciliation plan drafted to audit and credit customers for duplicated tokens in March invoices.
rollout_plan: Canary (dedicated-us-west cluster A) - 2026-03-08 - success metrics: no new duplicate events for 48h
Staged rollout (hosted infra) - 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11 - monitor 2x historical baseline windows
Full rollout (private deploy customer coordinations) - 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13 - provide agent for customers to apply patch or accept managed update
billing_reconciliation_plan: 1) Run a retro audit job to identify duplicated accounting events (logical_request_id missing historically) between 2026-02-20 and 2026-03-05.
2) Compute duplicated token delta per invoice and prepare credits for impacted customers; draft credits to be reviewed by Finance.
3) Offer a goodwill credit and 30-day free usage for affected enterprise customers (sales/CS to approve).
4) Publish an incident summary and notify customers with clear remediation and credit amounts by 2026-03-18.
support_communications: 2026-03-06 - Sent initial acknowledgement to customers via Account team. Advised we will pause billing for streaming token deltas while investigating (applies to suspected invoices).
2026-03-09 - Shared preliminary findings and mitigation steps; promised final reconciliation plan within 10 business days.
2026-03-11 - Updated customers: patch deployed canary, awaiting metrics for full confidence before applying credits.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add unit/integration tests for streaming-resume idempotency in runtime and aggregator (owner: runtime team).
2) Expand dedupe to consider session-resume tokens in ingestion pipeline (owner: aggregator).
3) Add telemetry that surfaces session_id churn rates per customer (owner: SRE).
4) Update public docs on streaming best-practices advising clients to persist resume tokens (owner: API docs).
5) Finance: finalize credit calculations and update billing infra to accept manual adjustments for affected invoices.
next_steps: Complete full rollout by 2026-03-12 and verify 7-day baselines.
Run the backfill audit and prepare credit letters for customers by 2026-03-18.
Execute postmortem and schedule retro with Platform, Runtime, SRE, and Finance (w/c 2026-03-22).
